Subject: Follow-up: geo constraints, PII flows, and retention questions (post-call)

Hi Ellen / Ravi —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discussion and the actions we promised to follow up on. I want to make sure we captured the constraints correctly so we can align the technical proposal and contract language.

Key constraints you outlined: 
- All customer PII used in inference must remain in US-based infrastructure; no processing in EU/APAC for this workload.
- Retention: operational logs retained for 90 days; request-level payloads purged within 30 days unless explicitly flagged for retention.
- Auditability: need exportable per-request logs with request id, timestamp, model version, and routing region.
- Cross-region failover allowed only to warm-standby within US regions; cross-border failover requires exec approval.

Next steps (tracked below):
1) We will send a compact region-matrix showing how pinning + failover behave for cold/warm standby. (Marcus / Aditya) — attached draft.
2) Monica will pull the SOC 2 extract and the logging schema we expose for exports.
3) You asked for a short note on how ephemeral KV caches and prefix caching are handled w.r.t PII — we will provide wording for the MSA.

Attachments: redwood-region-matrix.xlsx (draft), soc2-extract.pdf (relevant excerpts)

If anything above is off, flag it and we will correct. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — this is really helpful. A couple clarifications from our side before you draft contract language: 

1) When you say "request-level payloads purged within 30 days," does that include any transient caches (e.g., KV cache entries) that might contain PII-derived tokens? We need assurance those are not persisted to disk beyond the retention window.
2) For audit exports: do the per-request logs include payload hashes only or full payloads? Our compliance team prefers hashes where possible, but we may need full payloads in a limited window for incident investigation.
3) Regarding warm-standby: can you confirm the expected RTO/RPO numbers when failing over inside the US? We are looking for <5 min RTO for a warm standby and RPO of <1 minute if possible.

We can review the region matrix you attached and circle back. If you can draft the recommended MSA text for the PII/cache behavior that would speed things up.

—Ellen

Ellen —

Thanks for the precise questions. Short answers up front, followed by the technical caveats we should include in the MSA/SoW draft: 

1) KV and prefix caches: by default, Redwood keeps these in memory on the serving node; we do not write KV cache entries to durable disk unless a customer requests snapshotting for warm-start scenarios. For Nimbus's default setup (US-only, no snapshotting), caches are ephemeral and cleared as part of normal process restarts. We'll include an explicit clause that memory-only caches containing PII are treated as ephemeral and not persisted.

2) Per-request logs: our export can be configured two ways — (a) hashed payloads only (recommended), or (b) full payload export for a configurable short window (e.g., 30 days) with restricted access. We will propose the default as hashed payloads and offer an escalation path for full payload exports under documented incident procedures.

3) RTO/RPO for warm standby inside US: typical RTO is 3–7 minutes depending on model size and active batch draining; RPO achievable is ~30–90 seconds with continuous KV replication turned on. We'll put conservative SLs (RTO < 10m, RPO < 2m) and propose tighter operational targets as an addendum if Nimbus requires them.

Action items from engineering/security side: 
- I will attach our logging schema and the short SOC2 extract with relevant control mappings (see attachments).
- Aditya will produce a one-page MSA paragraph on caches + payload handling for legal to review.

LMK if you'd prefer different defaults.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Draft: short MSA paragraph on PII handling, caches, and failover

Ellen —

Per Monica's note, attached is a short draft snippet you can drop into the MSA/SoW. Comments welcome — I tried to cover the cache behavior, log exports, and failover constraints in plain language.

Attached: nimbus-map-draft.pdf (visual), redwood-region-matrix.xlsx, draft-msa-pii-paragraph.txt (in email body below).

--- draft MSA paragraph (start) ---
Redwood shall process and store customer-provided personal data used for inference exclusively in data centers located within the United States for the services covered by this agreement. Ephemeral in-memory caches (including KV caches and prefix caches) used to optimize inference are not persisted to durable storage unless explicitly configured and accepted in writing by the customer. Request payloads and generated outputs will be retained and accessible to the customer for a default period of thirty (30) days after submission, after which such payloads will be deleted. Operational logs necessary for debugging and audit purposes will be retained for a default period of ninety (90) days; log exports may be delivered as payload hashes by default, with full payload export available under a documented incident-response process subject to elevated access controls. Cross-border failover to non-US regions will not occur without prior executive-level approval; warm-standby failover between US regions is permitted per the warm-standby policy described in Appendix A.
--- draft MSA paragraph (end) ---

If that captures things, we can hand to legal and mark the MSA paragraph as 'customer review'.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
